event.citedText:
LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA S250818k: Properties of the low-significance GW compact binary merger candidate potentially associated with AT 2025ulz

The LIGO Scientific Collaboration, the Virgo Collaboration, and the KAGRA Collaboration (LVK) report:

We identified the compact binary merger candidate S250818k during real-time processing of data from LIGO Hanford Observatory (H1), LIGO Livingston Observatory (L1), and Virgo Observatory (V1) at 2025-08-18 01:20:06.030 UTC (GPS time: 1439515224.030).

Based on the analysis of gravitational-wave (GW) data alone, this candidate does not meet our criteria for a high-significance public alert as its false alarm rate is estimated by the online analysis to be 6.8e-08 Hz or about one in 5 months.

The GW candidate’s properties can be found at this URL:

https://gracedb.ligo.org/superevents/S250818k

The classification of the GW candidate, in order of descending probability, is Terrestrial (71%), BNS (29%), NSBH (<1%), or BBH (<1%).
Marginalized over the whole sky, the a posteriori luminosity distance estimate is 237 +/- 62 Mpc (a posteriori mean +/- standard deviation).
We derive a redshift of 0.0848 based on host galaxy emission lines - this is consistent with the 3D GW localization for S250818k.
The data in-hand thus far appears consistent with a kilonova.

We note significant reddening and fading from our previous report (GCN 41421), with the g band dropping 0.83 AB mag in 24.6 hours and r band now being brighter than g.

The magnitudes are calibrated against the PS1 catalog and not corrected for Galactic extinction.

answer.text: The LVK compact binary merger candidate S250818k was identified at 2025-08-18 01:20:06.030 UTC (GPS time: 1439515224.030), but it is a low-significance event: its false alarm rate is estimated by the online analysis to be 6.8e-08 Hz or about one in 5 months.
The classification is Terrestrial (71%), BNS (29%), NSBH (<1%), or BBH (<1%).
The updated analysis gives a posteriori luminosity distance estimate is 237 +/- 62 Mpc.

Keck I spectroscopy gives a redshift of 0.0848 based on host galaxy emission lines - this is consistent with the 3D GW localization for S250818k, and the data in-hand thus far appears consistent with a kilonova.
Follow-up showed significant reddening and fading from our previous report (GCN 41421), with the g band dropping 0.83 AB mag in 24.6 hours and r band now being brighter than g.
No high-energy counterpart has been reported.
The source was not detected with XRT with an upper limit of 3.8 * 10^-3 cts/s at 0.3 - 10 keV.
There was no Fermi-GBM onboard trigger around the event time of the LIGO/Virgo/KAGRA (LVK) detection of GW trigger S250818k.
